newsitem.title: THAILAND: Australians admit drugs charge in Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Australians admit drugs charge in Thailand.

text.p: Three Australians arrested seven months ago on charges of heroin trafficking pleaded guilty on Monday to possessing heroin but denied being involved in drug trafficking.
Lyle Doniger, 44, Jane McKenzie, 29, and Deborah Spinner, 29, all from Sydney, appeared in Bangkok criminal court in brown prison clothes on Monday for their first hearing.
Their case was postponed in August after a defence lawyer failed to appear.
They were arrested on March 22 as they were about to board a flight home after customs agents found 350 grams (12.5 ounces) of heroin in their posession.
On Monday, the three admitted possessing the heroin but they denied being involved in narcotics trafficking.

But a court official said their challenge to the trafficking charge would probably not be accepted. Under Thai criminal law, possession of more than 20 grams (0.7 ounces) of heroin is regarded as an attempt to traffic drugs.
Heroin trafficking carries the death penalty in Thailand but the sentence is invariably commuted to a lengthy prison term.
The court has set October 24 for the next hearing.
